lines.vo: Ever feel your phone buzz, grab it, and there's nothing there?
That's not a ghost in your pocket. That's your brain on buzz patrol.
Kev logs every fake buzz in his Break the Habit tracker.
In one study of about 290 college students, roughly 89 percent had felt phantom vibrations.
Most said it happened about every couple of weeks, and it barely bothered them.
One idea is your brain gets so primed for that buzz, it reads random twitches as alerts.
So cut the extra notifications, and give your brain fewer buzzes to wait for.
Fewer buzzes, more check marks. That's how you stay on track.
